proposals.old: Havens recognizes an organizational claim where alleged discriminatory conduct made the organization’s housing-referral work more costly.
proposals.new: Havens recognizes an organizational claim where alleged racial steering directly impaired the organization’s housing counseling and referral services. FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine (2024) distinguishes that interference from an organization’s choice to spend money investigating or opposing a policy; those expenditures alone do not establish injury.
proposals.reason: Prevent a simplified cost account from suggesting that voluntary advocacy-resource diversion itself establishes organizational standing.

proposals.old: A corporation is a citizen of its state of incorporation and of the state of its principal place of business (§ 1332(c)(1)).
proposals.new: A corporation is a citizen of every State and foreign state in which it is incorporated and of the State or foreign state where it has its principal place of business (§ 1332(c)(1)).
proposals.reason: Include all incorporating jurisdictions and foreign states instead of suggesting only a single domestic state.
proposals.status: applied as exact-old-text guarded runtime correction

proposals.old:
Klein v. PepsiCo, Inc.: The aircraft sale was binding, but available substitutes and adequate damages made specific performance inappropriate.

Walgreen Co. v. Sara Creek Property Co.: An injunction enforcing a shopping-center pharmacy exclusivity clause was justified because projecting ten years of competitive losses would be costly and uncertain.

Commonwealth v. Cosby: Fundamental fairness requires enforcement of an unconditional nonprosecution assurance when it induces detrimental surrender of the constitutional privilege against self-incrimination.

Additional assigned materials: French specific-enforcement reading; Economics of remedies video lecture.
proposals.new:
Klein v. PepsiCo, Inc.: The aircraft sale was binding, but available substitutes and adequate damages made specific performance inappropriate.

Walgreen Co. v. Sara Creek Property Co.: An injunction enforcing a shopping-center pharmacy exclusivity clause was justified because projecting ten years of competitive losses would be costly and uncertain.

In Commonwealth v. Cosby (Pa. 2021), the majority enforced the former prosecutor’s unconditional nonprosecution decision because it intentionally induced reasonable, detrimental surrender of Cosby’s Fifth Amendment protection in civil depositions. The decision concerns that record and these charges; it does not make every prosecutorial assurance enforceable.

Additional assigned materials: French specific-enforcement reading; Economics of remedies video lecture.
proposals.reason: Confine prosecutorial nonprosecution assurance to the actual Cosby record and detrimental constitutional reliance.

sources.pinpoint: majority opinion; canonical Cosby brief holding/reasoning
